# Advanced Source Deep-Dive Protocol

This is the execution protocol for real source inspection.

## Clone and inventory

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/agent-audit
cd /tmp/agent-audit
git clone --depth=1 <repo-url> repo
cd repo
printf "repo=%s\ncommit=%s\n" "$(git remote get-url origin)" "$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
find . -maxdepth 3 -type f | sort > FILE_INDEX.txt
```

## Classify source risk

```text
LOW: docs-only, examples-only, static reference list.
MEDIUM: CLI or scripts with local file access but no network/secrets.
HIGH: MCP server, hook, plugin, memory layer, dashboard, bridge, one-line installer.
CRITICAL: downloads binaries, modifies shell/profile, broad filesystem/network, hidden telemetry, credential access.
```

## Inspect dangerous surfaces

```bash
rg -n "curl|wget|bash|sh -c|sudo|chmod|chown|eval|exec|child_process|subprocess|spawn|postinstall|preinstall|install.sh" .
rg -n "MCP|mcp|tools|permissions|allowed-tools|deny|hook|PreToolUse|PostToolUse|Stop|Subagent" .
rg -n "token|secret|api_key|OPENAI|ANTHROPIC|GITHUB_TOKEN|DATABASE_URL|telemetry|analytics|sentry" .
rg -n "memory|sqlite|vector|embedding|qdrant|chromadb|weaviate|redis|postgres" .
```

## Keep/drop decision

Keep only if:

```text
purpose is clear
permission model is explicit
network/filesystem behavior is justified
telemetry is absent or opt-in
uninstall path exists
license is acceptable
maintainer activity is credible
candidate beats baseline benchmark
```

A 99-day-old repo shipping 15 commits/day is structurally different from a 99-day-old repo shipping 1 commit/week — the former is still in active iteration, not burn-in. Compute `cpd = total_commits / age_days` alongside age:\n\n| cpd × age band | Classification | Implication |\n|---|---|---|\n| `cpd < 10` AND `age ≥ 90d` | Stable burn-in | Firm axis-3 PASS |\n| `10 ≤ cpd ≤ 20` AND `90d ≤ age ≤ 180d` | Active iteration | Borderline axis-3 — PASS-with-caveat; downgrade to STUDY-PILOT or CONDITIONAL-ADOPT if axis-2 also PARTIAL |\n| `cpd > 10` AND `age > 180d` | **Sustained active maintenance** | Firm axis-3 PASS — mature age proves stability AND velocity signals ongoing investment, NOT rewrite churn. Classic shape: high-velocity repos past burn-in (avoid misclassifying as fast-churn anti-pattern) |\n| `cpd > 10` AND `age < 100d` | Fast-churn anti-pattern | Treat age-PASS as borderline, expect rewrites, re-audit after +90d |\n| **STRONG-PROVENANCE-EXPRESS** (5th band, predicate-gated): `age ≥ 30d` AND axis-1 = official-org maintainership AND axis-2 = named-T2 endorsement OR maintainer-org IS T2-equivalent | **Firm axis-3 PASS — relaxed maturity gate** | When provenance is strong (org-level T1) AND a named-T2 OR org-equivalent endorsement exists, the launch-spike risk that motivates the strict 90-day gate is dominated by maintainer-org commitment. Examples of org-level T1 patterns: vercel-labs / anthropics / openai / getzep / langchain / microsoft / google / facebook-research / google-deepmind / openai-evals / equivalents. The LAUNCH-SPIKE band still applies for `unknown-org + age<90d + cpd>50` — protection holds for the truly anti-pattern cases (solo-org launch with non-permissive license = REJECT-UNTIL-CONVERGENCE unchanged) |\n\nThe bands are exhaustive — every candidate falls into exactly one. STRONG-PROVENANCE-EXPRESS is a predicate-gated relaxation, not a default fallback; verify all three predicate clauses (≥30d age, official-org maintainer, named-T2 or org-equivalent endorsement) before applying it.\n\n### Fusion rule (Rider 4 discipline)\n\nNo single tool is authoritative. Running any ONE of the above in isolation produces narrow-grep false-negatives (single-tool signal ≠ convergence). The convergence check requires ≥3 distinct tool-types returning compatible evidence — otherwise treat the finding as \"one-tool signal,\" which is not convergence.\n\nCost discipline: cheap-first. `mcp__github__` calls (cheap, rate-limited) before `mcp__firecrawl__firecrawl_agent` (multi-minute credits). DeepWiki `ask_question` before packing the whole repo with repomix. If 3 cheap signals converge, don't escalate to expensive ones; if they don't converge, ONE expensive confirmatory signal is worth more than three more cheap ones.\n\n## Anti-pattern: retroactive convergence manufacturing\n\nDo not construct convergence evidence after choosing the verdict. The sequence must be: (1) collect convergence evidence → (2) count axes → (3) verdict. Not (1) pick verdict → (2) find supporting cites.\n\nIf a candidate looks promising but fails convergence today, the right move is to **queue a re-audit date** (90 days out, or when a named T2 practitioner is spotted adopting it), not lower the gate.\n\n## Anti-pattern: Row-2 fabrication-test FAIL\n\nWhen running the 5-row bar's Row 2 (Numeric — measurable improvement), a README presenting **≥3 numeric performance claims without methodology citation** (no repro script link, no benchmark repo, no dataset name) is **auto-FAIL** — do not attempt live A/B to verify, just REJECT. This short-circuits the primary-source rule: vendor marketing numbers that aren't backed by a reproducible artifact are false-by-default until proven otherwise.\n\n**Procedure**:\n1. Count numeric claims in README that make improvement/speedup assertions\n2. For each, check: does the README cite a reproducible artifact (benchmark script path, dataset name, tool+version)?\n3. If ≥3 claims lack citations, Row-2 auto-FAIL → REJECT verdict bypasses expensive verification step\n4. If 1-2 claims lack citations, run the live-verify anyway (lower signal-to-noise)\n5. If all claims cite reproducible artifacts, proceed to full primary-source check","numLines":35,"startLine":93,"totalLines":158}}
